page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-4 is an Arm-based compute instance built on the arm64 architecture, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, this configuration prioritizes compute throughput over memory footprint. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Resource allocation on this machine tier relies strictly on attached network block storage, as local SSDs are absent. Networking environments must also account for zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 cores deliver stable CPU capacity without virtualization oversubscription, lowering operational costs per core relative to high-memory architectures when workloads do not require large working sets.

Workloads best aligned with the c4a-highcpu-4 include containerized microservices, CPU-bound batch processing, continuous integration build runners, code compilation, and front-end web serving tasks that operate efficiently within an 8.0 GB memory envelope.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-4 is an arm64-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, resulting in a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Designed for compute-heavy execution, this instance provides dedicated processor scheduling without hyper-threaded resource sharing. It includes no local storage volumes and no hardware graphics accelerators, directing persistent storage needs entirely to attached persistent disk solutions. The instance is not provisioned with default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because of its constrained memory footprint relative to processing capacity, the c4a-highcpu-4 offers a cost-effective platform for workloads that demand predictable CPU execution without large caching requirements. Optimal applications comprise software build nodes, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, and distributed microservices tailored for the Arm instruction set architecture.
